boundary_decision.rationale: The model owns one journey identity, journey-scoped composition, assertions, state and correction lineage. Person, vehicle, organization, route, itinerary, network, place, service, schedule, booking, ticket, shipment, incident, sensor and evidence remain external masters.

decisions.rationale: A stable journey groups one intended or undertaken movement and its stages, typed clocks, observations and corrections without becoming a route, itinerary, service or subject.
Transmodel and GTFS demonstrate that passenger movement and a vehicle service run may be related but need separate identities, participants and counting rules.
A one-way purpose-bounded trip, a public-transport boarding and a wider journey away from home are not interchangeable without an explicit statistical or domain profile.
The journey references reusable paths and selected planning results, preserving actual deviation and successor plans without importing route or itinerary lifecycle.
A stage is generally mode-specific movement, a call is a visit to a point and a boarding is an event; none alone is the whole journey.

decisions.concept: Requested, planned, predicted, observed and actual time
decisions.rationale: Each clock has its own source, authority, operating-day and timezone basis and must survive reconciliation rather than last-write-wins.
A position sample is an observation; a trajectory is a time-qualified geometry that may include gaps and interpolation and cannot prove journey completion by itself.
Passenger Mobility / Transit is narrower by traveller and broader by networks, services and fares, so inheritance is not approved.
A shipment may cite transport journeys, while cargo, consignment and custody remain shipment-owned.
Delay, cancellation, diversion, interruption and missed connection qualify journey outcome but generic incident identity and authority remain external.
Transmodel, GTFS, OGC, ISO, UNECE, tourism statistics and Schema.org use different trip boundaries, vocabularies and conformance expectations.

publication_holds: Absence-of-external-review hold: one Claude Sonnet and one Grok attempt for WM-FLW-009 each timed out after 120 seconds; no external result was admitted.

Boundary hold: Journey owns one movement episode and its journey-scoped assertions while route, itinerary, person, vehicle, service, schedule, booking, ticket, shipment, incident, sensor and evidence masters remain external.
Relation hold: WM-FLW-007 remains a candidate compositional reference rather than an approved parent because its transit boundary does not equal generic Journey / Trip.
Neighbor hold: WM-FLW-010 currently combines Route / Itinerary; its reusable-route and planning-result boundaries need independent research and may require a future split.
Terminology hold: trip, journey, stage, leg, call, boarding, tour and travel have profile-specific meanings and require an explicit vocabulary profile.
Mode hold: pedestrian, bicycle, road, rail, maritime, aviation, private, shared, public, on-demand, freight-linked and autonomous-vehicle journeys need independently validated profiles.
Jurisdiction hold: safety, accessibility, passenger rights, border movement, privacy, employment travel, retention and evidence rules depend on region and context.

Segmentation hold: purpose changes, mode changes, vehicle changes, stopovers, overnight stays, loops, series of calls, interrupted trips and return journeys require profile-specific split and merge rules.
Observation hold: map matching, trajectory gaps, interpolation, sensor accuracy, identity matching and completion inference require tested methods and confidence thresholds.
Prediction hold: delay, ETA, rerouting and recovery views require model, input-cutoff, uncertainty, freshness and benchmark evidence.
Privacy hold: personal trips and live locations need purpose limitation, minimization, consent or other authority, protected access and deletion profiles.

Interoperability hold: every Transmodel, GTFS, OGC, ISO, statistical, Schema.org, GeoSPARQL, OWL-Time, PROV, DQV and ODRL projection needs exact release pins, conformance evidence and semantic-loss declarations.
Review hold: transport operations, mobility planning, geospatial, statistics, tourism, accessibility, safety, privacy, data governance, records and independent external review are outstanding.
Independent external review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this codex-only result remains a reviewable draft.
